subject: science
passage: On cold nights, many hummingbirds enter torpor, a state in which body temperature and metabolic rate drop sharply. Because a hummingbird burns energy so quickly that it could starve overnight, ornithologist Tadeusz Kowal describes torpor as an emergency measure. Birds resort to it, he argues, only when their fat reserves have fallen too low to fuel a night at normal body temperature.
passage_b: Ecologist Ana Mamani weighed hummingbirds at dusk on a high Andean slope and then recorded their body temperatures through the night. Birds of every species she studied entered torpor, including individuals that had gone to roost carrying ample fat. Mamani suggests that at such altitudes torpor is less a last resort than a routine strategy: by spending the night in torpor, a bird can save its reserves for the demands of the following day.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument made by Kowal in Text 1?

choices.A: By suggesting that only Andean species of hummingbirds are able to enter torpor
choices.B: By citing evidence that hummingbirds with sufficient reserves also enter torpor
choices.C: By agreeing that torpor is an emergency measure for hummingbirds at high altitudes
choices.D: By disputing that hummingbirds burn energy fast enough to risk starving overnight

explanation.why: Kowal claims hummingbirds use torpor "only when their fat reserves have fallen too low." Text 2 reports that torpor occurred even in "individuals that had gone to roost carrying ample fat," and Mamani calls torpor "less a last resort than a routine strategy." Text 2 would answer Kowal with evidence against his "only when" claim.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 studied Andean birds but never says other hummingbirds cannot enter torpor; Text 1 says many do.
explanation.B: Correct. Mamani's well-fed birds entered torpor too, which contradicts the claim that torpor occurs only when reserves run low.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 calls torpor at high altitude "less a last resort than a routine strategy," the opposite of an emergency measure.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 never questions how quickly hummingbirds burn energy.
